subject.title: /new and /reset should support @agent targeting in multi-agent channels

question: What should `/new` and `/reset` do in a multi-agent channel when no explicit agent target is supplied, and which target syntax should be accepted?
rationale: The implementation gap is clear, but choosing `@agent`, native `agent:` parameters, and ambiguous no-target behavior affects session-state safety, command authorization, and existing shared-channel workflows.

options.title: Require explicit target in shared rooms
options.body: Add text and native-command agent targeting, and make ambiguous destructive commands prompt or no-op instead of resetting a guessed agent.

options.title: Keep route default plus target override
options.body: Preserve current route/binding behavior when no target is supplied, while adding `@agent` or native `agent:` as an override.

options.title: Document channel isolation only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document dedicated channels, bindings, or per-account command naming as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Require explicit target in shared rooms
recommendation.body: Add text and native-command agent targeting, and make ambiguous destructive commands prompt or no-op instead of resetting a guessed agent.

likelyOwner.reason: The native command target helper and session-routing contract history point to this owner for the product/security boundary decision.
